capabilityIntro: Production drafting for utility closeout, legacy drawing conversion and civil CAD queues. Start with one to three representative sheets so the buyer’s reviewer can confirm fit before assigning a larger batch.
buyerRoles: Utility contractor closeout or project manager
Engineering or survey CAD production lead
Civil consultant assembling plan and profile sheets

capabilities.title: Record drawings from approved field redlines
capabilities.summary: Bring construction revisions into the approved base drawing and log questions that need a review decision.
inputs: Approved field markups with revision and sheet references
Editable base CAD and dependent references
Target sheet list, plot standards and handoff deadline
outputs: Revised native CAD and plotted sheet set in the agreed format
Exception log with sheet references and reviewer actions
checks: Compare incorporated changes with the approved markups
Validate affected layers, external references and plot readability
Keep unresolved dimensions and tie-ins visible for the buyer’s decision

capabilities.title: Legacy PDF and raster conversion
capabilities.summary: Rebuild legible archive drawings as editable linework organized by the buyer’s layer and block standards.
inputs: Readable scan or PDF and a known dimension reference
Required file version, layer naming and drawing conventions
Instructions for gaps, blurry symbols and conflicting dimensions
outputs: Visual overlay or plotted source comparison
checks: Calibrate against the supplied dimension and cross-check another known interval when available
Review line alignment, labels and units against the source

capabilities.title: Civil and survey drafting production
capabilities.summary: Prepare agreed plan, profile and existing-condition sheets from reviewed source data under the buyer’s template.
inputs: Reviewer-approved source data and point or feature codes
Horizontal reference, vertical datum and units
Sheet template, callout list and drafting instructions
outputs: Assigned AutoCAD or Civil 3D files in the agreed format
Plotted sheets and dependent file manifest
Source point and missing-data notes for assigned review
checks: Confirm source identifiers, units and coordinate handling
Reconcile profile station and elevation labels with approved inputs
Log unknown attributes and wait for reviewer direction where needed

capabilities.title: CAD overflow and revision control
capabilities.summary: Establish a shared revision queue and repeatable handoff after the first production batch is accepted.
inputs: Batch priorities, reviewers and revision cadence
outputs: Each dated production batch with revision status
Manifest for files, references and unresolved inputs
Batch closeout notes for the designated reviewer
checks: Compare each revised sheet with its approved instruction
Confirm working files and plotted sheets match the issue register
Capture approved revision requests and return open decisions to the owner

formats: Native AutoCAD DWG or agreed Civil 3D version for production work
Plotted PDFs with a named sheet index
CSV or spreadsheet revision and exception registers
Portable DXF for the website illustrations
requirements: One authorized source set with a current revision
Approved units, CAD template, plot layout and dependent file list
Named reviewer, target delivery date and secure handoff channel
boundaries: The buyer’s accountable reviewer handles field verification, survey determinations and interpretation of design intent.
Engineering approval, professional sealing and permitting remain with the designated accountable professionals.
An unclear source detail stays logged until the buyer directs its disposition.

projects.title: Utility trench closeout
projects.summary: One approved field offset carried into a three-sheet record set, with a pending tie-in assigned for review.
projects.imageAlt: Side-by-side utility field markup and revised record plan

comparison.label: Before · Field markup
comparison.alt: Source plan with a dashed marked-up 14-foot offset and a circled tie-in
comparison.caption: M-01 supplies the offset and station limits. M-02 asks for a tie-in dimension at 1+80.

comparison.label: After · Record plan
comparison.alt: Revised solid green route with the original alignment in gray and open issue E-01 at the right
comparison.caption: The approved offset is in the editable record geometry. E-01 stays open across the plan, detail and change register.

projects.context: A simulated closeout lead supplies a marked-up utility alignment and illustrative conduit elevations. The handoff includes the record plan, supplied profile and tie-in detail, with the original markup available for comparison.
constraints: Use feet in a fictional local grid. Stations follow the original baseline.
Incorporate the approved 14-foot shift between 0+60 and 1+20. Retain supplied profile elevations.
Keep the tie-in dimension at 1+80 open for the designated reviewer.

approach.title: Separate approved work from review items
approach.text: Carry approved markup M-01 into the record geometry. Tie M-02 to E-01 in the register and on the detail.

approach.title: Update the record geometry
approach.text: Move the route between the station limits, keep the original line on its own layer and retain the supplied conduit profile.

approach.title: Prepare the issue package
approach.text: Assemble UT-01, UT-02 and UT-03 as named CAD layouts and matching 11 × 17-inch PDF sheets, then index each sheet by its source and review status.

deliverables: Layered DXF with UT-01 record plan, UT-02 profile and UT-03 tie-in detail
Matching vector PDF set and the source markup PDF
Sheet index and a source-linked change register with the open issue
verification: Check the modeled 14-foot offset between 0+60 and 1+20.
Open the three named layouts and compare sheet IDs and revisions to the PDF set.
Trace E-01 at 1+80 back to M-02 and verify who owes the next decision.
projects.review: The draft demonstrates a review issue. For a live package, the designated reviewer supplies the tie-in dimension and approves the final record. The example uses fictional coordinates and elevations.

projects.title: Legacy PDF to editable CAD
projects.summary: A raster utility-room plan redrawn as layered CAD, with two scale checks and one unreadable equipment tag logged.
projects.imageAlt: Side-by-side archive scan and editable CAD redraw of a utility room

comparison.label: Before · PDF scan
comparison.alt: Sepia raster scan of a utility room with 48-foot and 32-foot dimension references
comparison.caption: The archive scan provides two readable dimension references. The equipment tag near the return run is indistinct.

comparison.label: After · Layered CAD
comparison.alt: Clean CAD redraw with wall outlines, visible utility lines and a red L-01 review callout
comparison.caption: Editable walls, door, equipment footprints and visible pipe runs, with the source-tag exception identified as L-01.

projects.context: A fictional facilities manager supplies a scanned utility-room PDF. The redraw uses the 48-foot room width for scale, the independent 32-foot depth for a perpendicular check and the visible equipment and piping for linework.
constraints: Use the 48-foot horizontal dimension to calibrate the redraw.
Use the separately labeled 32-foot vertical dimension to check scale in the other axis.
Retain the blurry tag location and log the missing identifier as L-01.

approach.title: Calibrate the source
approach.text: Match the known room width to 48 drawing units. Compare the perpendicular wall extent against the independent 32-foot dimension.

approach.title: Organize editable lines
approach.text: Separate the room bounds, door, visible piping and equipment footprints into named layers. Carry the unclear tag as a review callout.

approach.title: Record conversion rules
approach.text: Plot LEG-01 from the same geometry, then map each feature to its target layer and log the source issue for the records owner.

deliverables: LEG-01 layered DXF with one named drawing layout
Matching vector redraw PDF and original synthetic raster PDF
Source-to-layer crosswalk with open issue L-01
verification: Measure the editable room envelope at 48 by 32 feet in model space.
Compare the door, equipment and pipes in the source scan with the plotted redraw.
Find L-01 in the CAD layout and crosswalk, then identify the records owner’s next action.
projects.review: The draft demonstrates translation from a synthetic scan. On a live job, the records owner confirms the equipment tag and the approved source before release.

files.description: Matching vector drawing with the two dimension checks and open tag callout.

files.label: Synthetic archive scan
files.description: Raster-only source PDF with the legible room dimensions and the unclear equipment tag.

files.label: Source-to-layer crosswalk
files.description: CAD layers, dimension checks and the owner action for open tag L-01.

projects.title: Civil existing-conditions plan and profile
projects.summary: Five fictional source points produce a coordinated plan and profile with checked station and elevation labels.
projects.imageAlt: Synthetic civil drawing showing five centerline points over 100 feet and the corresponding existing elevation profile
projects.context: A fictional civil reviewer provides five existing-ground points along an access corridor. The sample turns them into a centerline plan and profile with enough source detail to reconcile each plotted label.
constraints: Use the supplied synthetic local planar coordinates and illustrative vertical datum.
Draft a 100-foot alignment at 25-foot source intervals.
Represent the profile at 10 times vertical exaggeration in its separate graphic frame.

approach.title: Validate the source import
approach.text: Check that source point IDs are unique and stations advance in 25-foot increments from 0+00 to 1+00.

approach.title: Draft plan and profile views
approach.text: Plot coordinates in the plan frame. Convert each supplied elevation to its profile height above the 100-foot datum line.

approach.title: Package the source for checking
approach.text: Retain the input register with source IDs, stations, coordinates and elevations so a reviewer can reconstruct the views.

deliverables: CV-01 editable DXF with plan and profile frames
Illustrated plan and profile preview with the vertical scale noted
verification: Check that the centerline spans 100 drawing units with five labeled points.
Confirm that the peak elevation is 101.20 feet at station 0+50 and plots 12 profile drawing units above the 100-foot datum line.
Check every annotated elevation against the downloaded point register.
projects.review: The client’s civil or survey reviewer would approve source, datum and drawing suitability. These fictional points have no survey provenance and are provided only for the workflow illustration.

files.label: CV-01 plan and profile drawing (DXF)
files.description: Layered centerline, point marks and a separate profile frame. Plan model units are feet.
